h1: The 5 Best Monitor Privacy Screens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Monitor Privacy Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five monitor privacy screens in 24 and 27 inch sizes, compared on magnetic mounting, 2-pack value and blue-light filtering.
summary: The 2 Pack 24 Inch Magnetic Computer Privacy Screen is the best monitor privacy screen, with magnetic attachment that switches between private and shared use. The Peslv 2-pack is the removable alternative, the 27 inch 2-pack is the only filter for bigger screens, and the SightPro adds anti-glare on a single 24 inch filter. The unbranded single is the cheapest way to test a filter.
intro: The commonest privacy-screen mistake is ordering the wrong size. A filter must match your monitor's diagonal and its 16:9 shape, and a near miss leaves a visible strip at the edge where someone beside you can read the screen. The product also works by narrowing the viewing angle, which means a head-on view stays clear and a sideways glance sees dark or blank.

Our editors compared five desktop filters from their listings, scored on the Primea framework, with fit, attachment method, pack size and extras like anti-glare weighted most. Prices are buckets only. None of these lists a dimming figure, so every pick darkens the picture by some unquantified amount, and an open-plan office is where the trade is worth making. Choose the pick that matches your monitor size first, then your habits.

products.name: 2 Pack 24 Inch Magnetic Computer Privacy Screen for Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.verdict: Magnetic attachment makes it easy to switch between private and shared use.
products.description:
This set includes two 24 inch widescreen filters that attach with magnets, in the $50 to $100 range. Magnets let you pull the filter off in a second when a colleague needs to see the screen, then snap it back. That is a practical advantage over stick-on or clip-on filters.

Magnetic mounting is the feature that puts it on top. Where the other filters hold in place or are described only as removable, this one is built for quick switching. Two in the box also covers a dual 24 inch desk.

Buy it if you switch between private and shared screen use. The caveats are the higher price bucket and the 24 inch limit. Skip it if you never need to remove the filter, because a fixed one costs less.
products.idealFor: People who switch between private and shared screen use.
products.skipIf: You never need to remove it.

products.name: Peslv [2-Pack] 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.verdict: A removable 24 inch pair with true side-angle privacy.
products.description:
The Peslv ships two 24 inch widescreen filters that are removable, with true side-angle privacy, in the $50 to $100 range. A removable filter can come off for presentations, though the listing does not describe how it attaches. For a dual-monitor desk, the pair covers both screens.

It lands just behind the magnetic set because removable here is not the same as magnetic. It still lets you take the filter off, and the price matches, but the attachment detail is thin, so you do not know how easily it comes off.

Buy it for dual 24 inch monitor setups. The caveats are the thin attachment detail and the higher price bucket. Skip it if you only have one monitor.

products.name: [2 Pack] 27 Inch Computer Monitor Privacy Screen, Blue Light Filter
products.verdict: The only 27 inch option here, with blue-light filtering built in.
products.description:
This is a 2-pack of 27 inch, 16:9 privacy screens that also filter blue light, in the $25 to $50 range. Blue-light filtering tints the display slightly, which some users like for late-night work and others find yellowing.

It is the only 27 inch pick in the roundup, which settles the order for anyone with a bigger monitor. It is also the cheapest pair, so the value is clear. The listing does not describe the attachment.

Buy it if you own 27 inch monitors. The caveats are that attachment is not described and that it fits only 27 inch screens. Skip it if you have a 24 inch monitor, because the size will not fit.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter for Monitor
products.verdict: A single 24 inch filter that adds anti-glare to side-angle privacy.
products.description:
The SightPro 24 Inch filter is a single 16:9 unit that offers true side-angle privacy plus anti-glare, in the $25 to $50 range. Anti-glare matters when a window or ceiling light throws reflections that make the dark filter look worse.

It comes fourth because it is one filter rather than a pair, but anti-glare is a feature none of the others list. For a single monitor in a bright office, it can beat the magnetic set on viewing comfort, though it lacks magnetic removal.

Buy it for a single 24 inch monitor in a bright room. The caveats are the single filter and no magnetic mount listed. Skip it if you need a pair.
products.idealFor: Single 24 inch monitors in bright rooms.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 24 Inch 16:9 Aspect Ratio Monitor
products.verdict: A no-frills single 24 inch filter for first-time buyers.
products.description:
This single 24 inch, 16:9 privacy filter offers true side-angle privacy, in the $25 to $50 range. It is the plainest option: one sheet, no extras, and an unbranded listing. For a first-time buyer, that makes the experiment cheap.

It finishes the list because it gives you the filter and nothing more. It is a fair way to test whether a privacy filter suits you before paying for a pair or a magnetic set, and it matches the SightPro on size.

Buy it for a low-cost trial on one 24 inch screen. The caveats are no extras and an unbranded listing. Skip it if you want a brand name or anti-glare.

whatMatters.detail: Filters are cut to a diagonal and aspect ratio. A mismatch leaves gaps or covers the bezel. Check your monitor's size and 16:9 ratio against the title, and measure the visible diagonal, not the box label, because a close-but-wrong filter leaves a bright strip that defeats its purpose. Shop by the diagonal you measured, then confirm the aspect ratio matches.

Magnetic filters come off in seconds, while permanent ones stay put. Choose by how often you share your screen. Look for the word magnetic or removable, as on the first two picks, and be aware that a filter without a stated method may use adhesive or clips. A fixed method suits a monitor that never changes hands, while magnets suit shared desks.

A 2-pack covers two monitors, which saves money on dual setups. A single covers one. Count your screens before buying, and remember that a pair means one for each screen at the same size, so mixed sizes need separate purchases. A cheap pair is wasted if one screen is a different size.

Anti-glare reduces reflections in bright rooms. Only the SightPro lists it here. Check for the word if your desk faces a window, since a dark privacy filter shows reflections more than a bare screen does, especially under overhead lights, and a glossy finish makes that worse. Matte filters hide fingerprints too.

Some filters also tint blue light. The 27 inch pack lists it. Treat it as a bonus, not a reason to buy alone, because the tint is mild and eye strain depends on habits more than a filter, and check whether you can tolerate a warmer tint, since it changes color accuracy for photo or design work. Skip the tint if color accuracy matters to you.

faq.q: Will it fit a curved monitor?
faq.a: The listings for these models do not mention curved screens. Check the product page before buying for a curved display, because a flat filter may not follow the curve. A rigid sheet on a curved screen leaves a gap.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Ordering the wrong size. Match the diagonal and the 16:9 ratio exactly, and measure before ordering, as the 24 inch and 27 inch listings here specify. A near miss is the commonest return.

faq.q: Is a magnetic filter worth it?
faq.a: If you share your screen often, yes. The magnetic 24 inch 2-pack lets you remove the filter in a second. Otherwise a fixed filter does the same job for less and stays put on the screen. Magnets add convenience, not extra privacy.
Follow the listing instructions. The magnetic pair attaches magnetically; for the others the listings do not describe the method, so read the product page. Ask the seller if the page is silent.

faq.q: Does it affect how my screen looks?
faq.a: Privacy filters can darken the view, which is the trade for side-angle privacy. The listings do not quantify it, so raise your brightness and expect a slightly dimmer image. Turn the brightness up before judging the filter.
Only if you have two monitors. A single filter like the SightPro is enough for one screen, and the 2-packs cover dual setups. Remember each pack needs matching sizes.

finalTake: Buy the magnetic 2-pack if you share your screen at times, and the Peslv if a removable pair suffices. The 27 inch pack is the only choice for larger monitors, and the SightPro is for a single screen in a bright room. The unbranded single is a low-cost trial. Check your diagonal and the 16:9 ratio against the title before ordering, because fit is the whole point.
